metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to code, pull requests, issues, and comments (explicitly named); 'any other contributions' as catch-all.
domains.accountability_holder: contributor (must verify/reproduce AI-assisted findings before filing issues; must not submit AI-generated code)

evidence.quote: Contributions must not include content generated by large language models or other probabilistic tools, including but not limited to Copilot or ChatGPT.
Can I submit a PR that includes code generated by AI tools? No.
you must verify the output of any AI tool before filing issues against the Servo project... you must be able to reproduce and validate any findings, not simply trust the tool's output.

domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly bans AI-generated code, PRs, issue text and comments, and places the burden of verification/validation on the contributor when using AI to assist in bug-finding. The maintainer close-PR clause is enforcement, not authorship accountability, so it is not used here; the verification language for issue-filing is the accountability statement.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots; no supervision or accountability stated
domains.reasoning: The file contains no reference to meeting recording, notetaker bots, or closed/small-group discussion capture by AI.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Documentation and non-code artifacts (comments, descriptions) explicitly named; blogs and design assets not mentioned.
domains.accountability_holder: contributor (non-code artifacts 'must be rewritten without the use of AI tooling')

evidence.quote: This policy covers code, documentation, pull requests, issues, comments, and any other contributions to the Servo project.
Any comments, descriptions, and other non-code artifacts that are not allowed by the previous FAQ entries must be rewritten without the use of AI tooling.

domains.reasoning: Documentation is explicitly named as within the AI ban, and non-code artifacts (comments, descriptions) must be rewritten without AI, placing responsibility on the contributor. Blogs and design assets specifically are not named, but the documentation/comment coverage is explicit enough for a 'yes'.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use in moderation actions; no accountability holder
domains.reasoning: The file discusses maintainers closing non-compliant PRs (enforcement of the AI policy itself) but does not address AI use in moderation decisions generally.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to using an AI tool to review one's own pull request; no volume limit stated.

evidence.quote: Can I use an AI review tool for my pull request? Yes, but please don't. The results are unreliable and noisy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for AI-assisted review
domains.reasoning: The policy names AI-assisted review of a contributor's own PR and permits it (discouraged but not banned, no disclosure requirement), but never states who is accountable for output produced this way, nor whether maintainers/reviewers themselves may use AI to review others' contributions.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on autonomous/agentic AI use; no supervision or accountability stated
domains.reasoning: No text addresses agentic or autonomous AI systems acting on the project's behalf; the policy only discusses tools used interactively by a human contributor.

domains.rationale_only_mention: AI tools require an unreasonable amount of energy and water to build and operate, their models are built with heavily exploited workers in unacceptable working conditions...
domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or rule; only cited as rationale for ban
domains.reasoning: Energy and water use are cited only as justification ('Ethical issues') for the code-contribution ban, not as a standalone rule governing environmental impact.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of infrastructure strain or hardware cost
domains.reasoning: The 'Maintainer burden' rationale discusses reviewer time and energy, a human/organizational burden, not server load or hardware/infrastructure cost; infrastructure strain is not mentioned anywhere in the file.

domains.rationale_only_mention: Publicly available models are trained on copyrighted content, both accidentally and intentionally, and their output often includes that content verbatim.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on training-data use; only cited as rationale for ban
domains.reasoning: Copyright/training-data provenance is raised only as a justification ('Copyright issues') for banning AI-generated contributions; no rule is set about data used to train models or about the project's own data being used for training.

unscoped_statements.quote: This policy covers code, documentation, pull requests, issues, comments, and any other contributions to the Servo project.
Contributions must not include content generated by large language models or other probabilistic tools, including but not limited to Copilot or ChatGPT.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Servo's getting-started guide is highly specific and restrictive about AI in code, documentation, issues, and comments (banned, contributor-accountable), permits but discourages AI-assisted self-review with no accountability holder named, and is silent on notetaker bots, moderation, autonomous/agentic use, infrastructure strain, and training data, mentioning environmental and copyright concerns only as rationale for the ban rather than as standalone rules.

validation_problems: code_contributions: quote not found in src/contributing/getting-started.md

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
